Deployment & Self-Hosting ​

This page covers running Saidi on a machine you control: what the build pipeline produces, how the server binds and serves the UI, what the supervisor does, and a step-by-step self-host procedure. It assumes you have already read Installation — this page is the production counterpart to it.

System requirements ​

RequirementValueWhere it comes from
Node.js>= 20engines.node in package.json
MongoDBRequired — the server refuses to boot without itsrc/orchestrator/server.ts exits 1 when connectMongo() fails
gitNeeded by any project agent that touches a repoagents shell out to git
ripgrepInstalled in the container image alongside gitDockerfile
DockerOnly if you enable the agent sandbox (SAIDI_SANDBOX=1)src/orchestrator/sandbox/docker.ts

The published container image is built on node:22-slim. The server bundle is compiled with an esbuild target of node20, so plain Node 20 is the floor.

Build pipeline ​

Everything is driven by npm scripts in the root package.json. Nothing here uses a Makefile or a task runner.

ScriptCommandProduces
setupnpm install && npm --prefix client installServer + client node_modules
build:clientnpm --prefix client run buildclient/dist/ (Vite production build of the React app)
build:servernode scripts/build-server.mjsdist/server.js (single minified ESM bundle)
buildbuild:client then build:serverBoth of the above
build:distnode scripts/build-dist.mjsstaging-dist/ — the source-free publishable package
build:allbuild then build:distBoth
build:sandbox-workernode scripts/build-sandbox-worker.mjsdist/sandbox-worker.js (entrypoint for the sandbox image)
preparenpm --prefix client install && npm run buildRuns automatically on npm install

What build:server does ​

scripts/build-server.mjs bundles src/orchestrator/server.ts into dist/server.js with esbuild: format: "esm", target: "node20", minify: true, and packages: "external". Keeping npm packages external means mongoose and the claude CLI the Claude Agent SDK spawns resolve from node_modules at the destination exactly as they do from source — so node_modules must be present next to dist/server.js at runtime. The bundle is not standalone.

The script also installs a small resolve plugin: the TypeScript source uses NodeNext-style .js import specifiers that point at .ts files on disk, and the plugin maps ./foo.js to the sibling ./foo.ts when it exists.

What build:dist does ​

scripts/build-dist.mjs assembles staging-dist/ from artifacts that must already exist — it throws if dist/server.js or client/dist/index.html is missing. The staging tree contains only dist/, client/dist/, bin/saidi.js, bin/supervisor.js, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, and a minimal package.json carrying runtime dependencies only (no tsx, no esbuild, no typescript) with a single script: start: node dist/server.js. As a guard, the script walks the staging tree and throws if any .ts/.tsx file leaked in.

build:dist is a packaging step for publishing, not something you need in order to self-host from a checkout.

The prepare hook ​

npm install at the repo root fires prepare, which installs the client dependencies and then runs the full build. That is why the Dockerfile gets a built server and client from a bare npm install, and why it asserts test -f dist/server.js && test -d client/dist immediately afterwards — so a broken build fails the image instead of shipping an empty one.

Running in production ​

bash
npm run build      # client/dist + dist/server.js
npm run start:prod # node dist/server.js

npm start (tsx src/orchestrator/server.ts) runs the same server from TypeScript source and is the development path; production uses the bundle.

The supervisor ​

bin/saidi.js is the saidi CLI entry and a supervisor around the server process. It:

  1. chdirs to the package root, because src/orchestrator/config.ts derives ROOT from process.cwd() and .env plus client/dist are resolved relative to it.
  2. Chooses the runtime: dist/server.js under plain Node when the bundle exists and SAIDI_DEV is unset, otherwise node --import tsx src/orchestrator/server.ts.
  3. Spawns the server as a child with SAIDI_SUPERVISED=1 and SAIDI_RUNTIME=dist|src in its environment.
  4. Opens the OS default browser once, on the first launch only, after polling the port for a TCP connection (skipped when SAIDI_DEV is set).
  5. Forwards SIGINT/SIGTERM to the child.

The restart rules live in bin/supervisor.js as a pure decideRestart() function:

Child exit codeSupervisor action
75 (RESTART_EXIT_CODE)Relaunch — the server asked for a fresh boot after a settings change
76 (UPDATE_EXIT_CODE)Run npm i -g github:saeed9321/saidi-agent, then relaunch
Anything elsePropagate the code; do not relaunch

A crash-loop guard stops after MAX_RESTARTS = 3 relaunches inside WINDOW_MS = 10_000. After an update, a rollback safety net reinstalls the previous version if the new child dies before HEALTHY_MS = 60_000; it is one-shot, so a second failure propagates normally.

Because the old child fully exits before the new one spawns, the port is always released before it is rebound.

Port, host, and reverse proxies ​

src/orchestrator/config.ts resolves every configurable value through one precedence rule:

  1. Genuine environment — a variable the real OS/container/shell set before .env was loaded (captured as a snapshot at module load). Always wins.
  2. The store — settings hydrated from MongoDB and installed via configureBindSettings() right before listen().
  3. .env at the package root — a dev convenience, lowest real priority.
  4. Built-in default.
ValueEnv varDefault
PortPORT4317
HostHOST127.0.0.1

The default bind is localhost only. To reach Saidi from another machine you must set HOST=0.0.0.0 (that is exactly what docker-compose.yml does) and put something in front of it — the repo does not ship a TLS terminator.

Things a reverse proxy in front of Saidi has to handle, based on what the server actually does:

  • WebSocket upgrades. src/orchestrator/server.ts attaches the streaming WebSocket to the same http.Server as the API, so the proxy must forward Upgrade/Connection headers on the same origin.
  • trust proxy. src/orchestrator/app.ts calls app.set('trust proxy', 1)only in cloud mode (SAIDI_CLOUD=1), where the comment names nginx explicitly. In local mode no proxy hop is trusted.
  • Origin checks. The cloud auth stack's CSRF guard compares the request Origin host against the inbound Host header or against SAIDI_PUBLIC_URL. If your proxy rewrites Host, set SAIDI_PUBLIC_URL to the browser-facing origin or mutating requests are rejected with 403.
  • Health. /api/health stays reachable when MongoDB is down; every other /api route returns 503 { ok: false, error: 'MongoDB unavailable' }. Use /api/health for proxy and supervisor health checks.

The repo ships no nginx, systemd, or pm2 configuration

There is no .service unit, no ecosystem.config.js, no Procfile, and no nginx snippet anywhere in the tree. The only process-management artifacts that exist are bin/saidi.js (the supervisor) and the Docker files below. If you want systemd or pm2, you write that unit yourself.

Where the client is served from ​

src/orchestrator/app.ts defines CLIENT_DIR = path.join(ROOT, 'client', 'dist') where ROOT is process.cwd(). With SAIDI_DEV unset, the server mounts express.static(CLIENT_DIR) and adds an SPA fallback that serves client/dist/index.html for any non-/api GET. If index.html is missing the server answers 503 Client not built. Run 'npm run build'.

With SAIDI_DEV set, the server serves no frontend at all — it 302-redirects any non-/api GET to the Vite dev server (SAIDI_CLIENT_URL, or http://<hostname>:5317). SAIDI_DEV must be unset in production.

Environment and secrets ​

MongoDB is the source of truth for settings and secrets; almost everything is configurable from the Settings UI. The variables below are the ones the code actually reads from the environment.

VariablePurpose
MONGODB_URIBootstrap connection string. This is the one credential that cannot live in Mongo. The database name is overridden by the mode (saidi local, saidi_cloud when SAIDI_CLOUD=1); default server is mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017
SAIDI_HOMEAbsolute path to the persistent data directory. Read before .env is parsed, so it must be a genuine env var. Falls back to ~/.saidi (or the repo root when SAIDI_DEV is set)
PORT / HOSTBind address, as above
ANTHROPIC_API_KEYAnthropic credential for the Claude Agent SDK
CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKENAlternative Claude credential (used in the container images, where interactive login is impossible)
SAIDI_CLOUD1 enables multi-tenant cloud mode: auth stack, org scoping, trust proxy
SAIDI_MASTER_KEY32-byte key (64 hex chars, or base64) used to envelope-encrypt secrets at rest. Required in cloud mode; without it the server warns at boot and encryption is off
SAIDI_PUBLIC_URLThe browser-facing origin, for the CSRF origin check behind a proxy
SAIDI_SANDBOX1 runs agent delegations inside Docker containers
SAIDI_SANDBOX_IMAGESandbox image tag; defaults to saidi-sandbox:latest
CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIRWhere the Claude SDK keeps session state — point it at your persistent volume in a container
SAIDI_DEVDevelopment only. Keeps state repo-local and disables static serving

SAIDI_SUPERVISED and SAIDI_RUNTIME are set by bin/saidi.js for its child; you do not set them yourself.

A root .env is optional. src/orchestrator/config.ts parses it if present, but only injects values the real environment left unset, and the Mongo-backed store outranks it.

The agent sandbox ​

If you set SAIDI_SANDBOX=1, the server preflights it at boot and warns loudly when the Docker daemon is unreachable or the image is missing — delegations fail until it is fixed. The build command the server itself prints is:

bash
npm run build:sandbox-worker
docker build -f src/orchestrator/sandbox/Dockerfile -t saidi-sandbox:latest .

With the sandbox off, agents run in-host. The env allow-list still withholds host secrets from them, but filesystem isolation between orgs requires the sandbox.

Self-hosting from a source checkout ​

  1. Install Node 20+ and a reachable MongoDB.

  2. Clone the repo and install both dependency trees:

    bash
    git clone https://github.com/saeed9321/saidi.git
cd saidi
npm run setup

  3. Decide where persistent state lives and export it before anything else. This directory must be outside the package, or a future update wipes it:

    bash
    export SAIDI_HOME=/var/lib/saidi

  4. Provide the bootstrap connection string and a model credential:

    bash
    export MONGODB_URI=mongodb://127.0.0.1:27017
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...

  5. Build:

    bash
    npm run build

  6. Choose a bind address. Keep the 127.0.0.1 default if a reverse proxy on the same host will front it; use HOST=0.0.0.0 only when something else terminates TLS and restricts access.

    bash
    export HOST=127.0.0.1 PORT=4317

  7. Start it:

    bash
    npm run start:prod

    Or run node bin/saidi.js instead, to get the supervisor (self-restart on settings changes, crash-loop guard, update install between spawns).

  8. Confirm the boot: the server logs MongoDB connected: …, prints a boot summary, and prints the URL to open. GET /api/health should answer even before you log in.

  9. Finish configuration in the UI under Settings — providers, secrets, scan roots. See Configuration.

Keep SAIDI_DEV unset throughout. Verify with npm run typecheck and npm test before pointing Saidi at anything you care about.

Self-hosting with Docker ​

The repo ships two compose files and one Dockerfile.

docker-compose.yml builds Saidi from the local source checkout and brings up three services: mongo (mongo:7), 9router, and saidi. The Dockerfile installs git, curl, ca-certificates, ripgrep, and tini, runs npm install (which triggers prepare, so the client and server are built inside the image), asserts both artifacts exist, exposes 4317, and runs node dist/server.js under tini.

bash
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
docker compose up -d --build

docker-compose.dist.yml is self-contained: its inline Dockerfile clones the prebuilt public distribution repo at a pinned SAIDI_REF, runs npm install --omit=dev, drops to uid 1000, and starts node bin/saidi.js so the supervisor handles restarts. Upgrading means bumping SAIDI_REF and re-running docker compose up -d --build.

Both files set the same production-critical environment inside the container:

yaml
HOST: "0.0.0.0"          # the 127.0.0.1 default is unreachable from outside
PORT: "4317"
SAIDI_HOME: /data        # read before .env — must be a real env var
SAIDI_CLOUD: "0"
MONGODB_URI: mongodb://mongo:27017

Persistent state is not in the image

/data holds config/, memory/, agents/, and run artifacts. Mount a volume there (both compose files use a named saidi-data volume) or you lose settings, secrets, and run history on every rebuild. Mongo needs its own volume too.

The compose files also publish 9Router on 20128 for provider routing, and note that the Saidi endpoint must be set in Settings → AI Providers, not as an env var, because applyModelProviderEnv in src/orchestrator/secrets.ts overrides ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL even when it is a genuine container env var.

Do not use the in-app "Update available" dialog inside a container: it would npm i -g over the image layer and the change would vanish on the next recreate. See Backups & Upgrades for the container upgrade path.

Troubleshooting a deployment ​

  • ✖ MongoDB is required — refusing to boot without it. — the bootstrap MONGODB_URI is wrong or the server is unreachable. There is deliberately no degraded file-backed mode.
  • Client not built. Run 'npm run build'. — client/dist/index.html is missing relative to process.cwd(). Check that you started from the package root.
  • Saidi restarted repeatedly in a short window — the crash-loop guard tripped. Revert your most recent Settings/Secrets change and start again.

More symptoms and fixes: Troubleshooting.
